summary: Three supported defects affect nine criteria: incomplete repository capture, omitted prior reviewer evidence, and blocked resumption of mirrored unsupported records. Twelve criteria pass.

criteria.title: AC1: planning and milestone authority
criteria.explanation: Planning and authority checks are present, but F1 permits acceptance and protected merging with review evidence that omits part of the application repository.

criteria.title: AC1: model-led execution
criteria.explanation: Readiness only records a declaration. Gate execution is explicit, genuine Verification inputs remain required, and no remediation counter or incidental execution graph imposes an order.

criteria.title: AC2: canonical layouts
criteria.explanation: Canonical records use the same local storage contract inside a repository or in a parent without Git. Tracking and ignore status do not control evidence admission, and finalization does not require evidence commits.

criteria.title: AC2: exact source and requirements
criteria.explanation: F1: configured repository paths are checked as directories, not Git roots. Running ls-tree from an accepted subdirectory captures only that subtree while binding the enclosing repository's full commit IDs.

criteria.title: AC2: containment and isolation
criteria.explanation: Canonical capture rejects traversal, symlinks, unsupported types and replacement during reads. Reviewer views materialize declared inputs as read-only files, preserve Git links as metadata, and request restricted fresh provider execution.

criteria.title: AC2: publication and retention
criteria.explanation: Exclusive publication, verified references, mirrored journals and retained job outcomes prevent incomplete or conflicting artifacts from becoming proof. Loss remains visible, repeat operations reconcile, and retention guidance distinguishes local copies from backup.

criteria.title: AC2: local finalization
criteria.explanation: Local reference closure is implemented, but F1 permits a packet covering a subtree to authorize a whole-repository PR. The Git-root check in integration verification occurs after the merge write.

criteria.title: AC3: independent grouped verdicts
criteria.explanation: Code/spec sharing retains separate validated verdicts. Fresh-context, capability, provider, input/output digest and receipt bindings are checked; missing verdicts and inherited implementing contexts do not qualify.

criteria.title: AC3: complete obligation inventory
criteria.explanation: The enabled obligations remain explicit with distinct roles, including Judge, packet, finalization, release and retention. Runner PASS requires matching successful receipts from recorded service jobs.

criteria.title: AC4: equivalent-input reuse
criteria.explanation: For correctly captured inputs, reuse compares content and qualification while preserving original result references and execution provenance. Bookkeeping and identical-content commits can reuse proof.

criteria.title: AC4: relevant change and uncertainty
criteria.explanation: F1 makes changes outside an accepted Git subdirectory invisible to content identity. Such application or shared-helper changes can therefore be treated as equivalent instead of invalidating affected proof.

criteria.title: AC4: targeted delta coverage
criteria.explanation: Delta validation checks declared changed paths and interactions, but F1 removes enclosing-repository paths before changedPaths is calculated. A delta can consequently claim complete coverage while omitting real changes in the same pinned repository.

criteria.title: AC5: bounded history and dispositions
criteria.explanation: F2: automatic history is selected through structured blocking findings. A valid prior criterion-only FAIL or required coverage limitation with no blocking finding is omitted from the next default assessment. Relevant reports from another gate also require manual selection.
evidence: Read-only in-memory executeGates probe: prior spec FAIL for R1 plus a required coverage limitation produced history=[] and reconsiderClosures=[].

criteria.title: AC5: new discovery and blocking criteria
criteria.explanation: Evaluator instructions explicitly permit new defects and new instances of resolved classes. Blocking findings require a selected approved criterion or gate rule and a source path in scope; advice remains distinguishable.

criteria.title: AC6: one scoped human decision
criteria.explanation: Observed instructions support combined decisions and expressly named continuations. Pending records grant no authority, identical retries reconcile, optional provenance is preserved, and amendments retain old/new documents.

criteria.title: AC6: honest exceptions and integration
criteria.explanation: Original verdicts and actual integration remain separate, but F1 also affects exception scope: unchanged partial-tree applicability can carry a waiver across a relevant change elsewhere in the enclosing repository.

criteria.title: AC7: enforcement coverage
criteria.explanation: Hook limitations are reported honestly, but F1 reaches the protected merge adapter: it validates partial captured proof against full PR commit IDs without rejecting the non-root repository path before execution.

criteria.title: AC7: coherent consumers and low ceremony
criteria.explanation: CLI, native plugins and desktop consume the same current core. Operations generate records, readiness does not launch evaluation, and shipped desktop controls expose obligations instead of the retired ordering graph.
evidence: All 23 desktop protocol files byte-match canonical protocol files.

criteria.title: AC8: direct cutover
criteria.explanation: The distribution uses the current core, removes the old orchestration resources and rejects retired merge execution. Current-entry views provide resume guidance, without migration, pilot or benchmark admission machinery. F3 concerns whether that resume operation succeeds.

criteria.title: AC8: resume without false history
criteria.explanation: F3: two identical activation copies bearing an unsupported contract are rejected as conflicting. Mutating preflight performs this rejection before dispatching run.resume-current, so explicit resume cannot establish a new run while preserving those records.
evidence: cli/test/current-core.test.js:583 removes the witness before testing unsupported-contract resume.
Read-only in-memory CurrentStore probe: identical unsupported primary/witness bytes returned 'Conflicting unsupported activation record'.

criteria.title: AC8: practical observations
criteria.explanation: Receipts retain execution times and available usage, missing metric contributions remain null, and current views preserve outcomes and exceptions separately. Workflow guidance describes real-project observation without a new metrics gate.

scopeCheck.explanation: The changed work stays within the approved core, helper, schema, CLI, native-plugin, desktop-consumer, test and documentation scope. No unrelated application deployment or publication change was identified.

gapCheck.explanation: Missing safeguards are Git-root validation before capture and merge, automatic retention of relevant criterion failures and coverage limits in reviewer packets, and an explicit resume path for matching unsupported activation copies.
evidence: The supplied verification scenarios do not cover these three cases.

contradictionCheck.explanation: The reachable behavior conflicts with the approved source-scope, applicability, reviewer-knowledge and current-resume contracts.
evidence: Spec C2/C4 require independently pinned application source and refreshed proof for relevant changes; F1 can bind only a subtree to full repository commits.
Spec C3 requires prior reviewer results and coverage limits; F2 omits valid prior failed assessments by default.
Spec C5 requires usable current entry for unsupported old state; F3 rejects matching retained copies before resume dispatch.

The protected merge still operates on the enclosing repository's complete PR. Integration verification rejects the non-root directory only after the merge write.

markdown:
**FAIL — three supported defects affect nine criteria; twelve criteria pass.**

This assessment covers the full approved rubric at FEATURE_FINAL for pinned head `257b22e65bd2ff7b70216b3b4985c91c54c88c16`, against base `643e3ea2b03f19b66595219c4f8df934596aa436`.

The specification, design, inventory, full Verification report and runtime attachment match their bound digests. All 49 patch chunks and the assembled patch material verify. The inventory contains 307 changes: 100 modified, 157 deleted and 50 added, with no renames or binary entries. All 150 retained new-file contents match the inventory blob IDs. All 23 desktop protocol files match canonical source.

**F1 — partial repository capture can authorize a whole-repository PR.** The resolver accepts a configured repository path when it is a contained directory; it does not establish that the directory is the Git root. Capture then runs `git ls-tree -r -z` from that directory without `--full-tree`. For a configuration pointing at `app/subdir`, source outside that subtree is omitted even though the manifest names commits from the entire `app` repository.

This omission propagates: an enclosing-repository source or shared-helper change can leave the captured content identity unchanged, disappear from delta paths, and preserve a content-scoped waiver. The protected adapter can then merge the complete PR using that partial review evidence. The Git-root guard in integration verification runs after the merge write. This is a static trace of the supplied source, not a hosted merge reproduction. Evidence: `protocol/context.js:158`, `current/evidence.js:57,168`, `current/execution.js:40`, `current/contracts.js:97`, `current/actions.js:89`, and `scripts/merge_verified.py:100`, under `plugin-src/shared/resources/`.

**F2 — default reviewer history omits valid prior failures and limits.** A spec/Judge FAIL may contain failed criterion rows or required coverage limitations without a structured blocking finding. Automatic history selection follows blocking-finding records, so that prior report is absent from the next default assessment unless manually selected. The requested-gate filter also excludes relevant reports from other gates by default.

A read-only in-memory call through the actual `executeGates` function, with stubbed state/store and qualification, confirmed that a prior spec FAIL for R1 plus a required integration limitation produced `history=[]` and `reconsiderClosures=[]`. No evaluator or filesystem publication was launched. Evidence: `current/execution.js:234,288,291,303`.

**F3 — matching unsupported activation copies block explicit resume.** `activationHead` treats an unsupported activation as opaque provenance only when its witness is absent. Two identical retained copies are rejected as conflicting. Because mutating preflight invokes this check before dispatching `run.resume-current`, the documented resume operation cannot establish a fresh current run from that state while preserving the records.

A read-only in-memory `CurrentStore` probe confirmed the error `Conflicting unsupported activation record` for matching unsupported primary/witness bytes. The existing unsupported-version test removes the witness first. Evidence: `current/store.js:175`, `current/core.js:580`, and `cli/test/current-core.test.js:583`.

| Criterion | Result | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| R1 — Planning and milestone authority | FAIL | F1 permits acceptance/merge with incomplete repository proof. |
| R2 — Model-led execution | PASS | Explicit readiness and evaluation; real input needs remain; no round cap. |
| R3 — Canonical layouts | PASS | Repository-local and parent/no-Git records use optional Git tracking. |
| R4 — Exact source and requirements | FAIL | F1 binds partial trees to whole-repository commit identities. |
| R5 — Containment and isolation | PASS | Safe capture and declared read-only reviewer views are implemented. |
| R6 — Publication and retention | PASS | Exclusive publication, integrity checks and repeat/crash reconciliation preserve proof boundaries. |
| R7 — Local finalization | FAIL | F1 defeats complete source/PR protection before the merge write. |
| R8 — Independent grouped verdicts | PASS | Fresh qualification and separate code/spec verdicts are validated. |
| R9 — Complete obligation inventory | PASS | Required gates and proper execution roles remain explicit. |
| R10 — Equivalent-input reuse | PASS | Correctly captured equivalent inputs reuse original proof and provenance. |
| R11 — Relevant change and uncertainty | FAIL | F1 can conceal relevant changes outside the captured subdirectory. |
| R12 — Targeted delta coverage | FAIL | F1 removes real changed paths before delta coverage validation. |
| R13 — Bounded history and dispositions | FAIL | F2 omits prior criterion failures and coverage limits by default. |
| R14 — New discovery and blocking criteria | PASS | New supported defects remain reportable under approved criteria. |
| R15 — One scoped human decision | PASS | Combined decisions, pending state, provenance and repeat-safe amendments are implemented. |
| R16 — Honest exceptions and integration | FAIL | F1 can preserve exception applicability across a relevant omitted source change. |
| R17 — Enforcement coverage | FAIL | The protected merge adapter does not reject F1 before execution. |
| R18 — Coherent consumers and low ceremony | PASS | CLI/plugins/desktop share the current core; obsolete ordering controls are removed. |
| R19 — Direct cutover | PASS | One current execution path and resume guidance replace retired orchestration. |
| R20 — Resume without false history | FAIL | F3 blocks the current entry for matching unsupported activation copies. |
| R21 — Practical observations | PASS | Available metrics and outcomes remain truthful; no new benchmark gate is introduced. |

**Scope check: PASS.** The changed work remains within the approved implementation, consumer, helper, test and documentation scope.

**Gap check: FAIL.** Repository-root validation, complete relevant reviewer-history selection, and matching-copy unsupported resumption are missing safeguards.

**Contradiction check: FAIL.** F1 conflicts with C2/C4 source and applicability requirements; F2 conflicts with C3 reviewer knowledge; F3 conflicts with C5 current resumption.

The full bound Verification report was read. It reports 317 CLI passes and one skip on an earlier substantive revision, eleven focused final regressions, 172 desktop passes, 58 reused Python passes, a real fresh evaluator execution, plugin validation and package/runtime checks. Its stated limits remain applicable: native host interception is unverified, runtime smoke covered ARM64, and exact-current hosted CI was unavailable. The bound `runtime.png` was visually inspected. These mechanical checks do not cover F1–F3. No code was edited and no network tools were used.
